# `sdf.mesh`: SDF shape

Builds an organic shape from named primitives blended in order (smooth unions, cuts) into a closed quad mesh.

- Category: sdf
- Version: 1
- Complexity: O(v x shapes) for the v voxels near the surface (about area / detail^2 x 8), parallel
- Flags: undoable, creates_groups, creates_objects
- Also known as: sdf, metaballs, sculpt, blob, implicit surface, csg, smooth union, volume modeling, clay

The sculpting tool for agents: write the shapes in order, each one primitive (`sphere`, `ellipsoid`, `box` with `corner` rounding, `capsule` with an optional `radius_b` taper, `cone`, `torus`, `cylinder`, or a `group` of shapes) plus how it joins the shapes before it: union (default), `smooth_union` with a fillet size, `subtract`, `smooth_subtract`, `intersect` or `smooth_intersect`. Each shape can be turned (`rotate`, degrees), grown (`round`), hollowed (`shell`), twisted or bent (degrees per meter), given seeded bumps (`noise`), and mirrored across the part's planes (`mirror: "x"` keeps the +x side and reflects it: write the left ear, get both).

Every face joins a group named after the shape that made it (`name`, or `shape_<n>`), so perception and diagnostics can name the shapes. `detail` is the voxel size, about the edge length of the result; walls thinner than a voxel make the mesher refine on its own.

A shape with `hidden: true` is left out but stays in the list (the others keep their group names). With `target`, the shapes rebuild that mesh object in place (it keeps its name, transform, parent and children): the object's history then holds the shapes to edit and run again.

**Use for** heads, bodies, creatures, rocks, organic props and stylized forms: blocking out with ellipsoids and capsules, then blending detail in. Hard-surface parts are better built with primitives, extrusions and bevels.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `detail` | `Length \| null` | - | Voxel size, about the edge length of the result: smaller is finer. The default fits about 64 voxels across the largest side. |
| `name` | `string \| null` | - | Object name; a free name such as `sdf_1` is picked when omitted. |
| `parent` | `string \| null` | - | Parent object (name, path or id); top level when omitted. |
| `position` | `[Length, Length, Length] \| null` | - | Origin position in the parent's space. |
| `shapes` | `SdfShape[]` | required | The shapes in order: each joins the shapes before it. |
| `target` | `string \| null` | - | Mesh object to rebuild in place from the shapes (it keeps its name, transform, parent and children) instead of making a new object. |

## Examples

```json
{"detail":"1cm","name":"blob","shapes":[{"name":"body","sphere":{"at":[0,0.1,0],"radius":0.1}},{"name":"head","smooth_union":0.03,"sphere":{"at":[0,0.21,0],"radius":0.06}}]}
```

Result: `created blob (o:4) sdf 0.1997 x 0.2697 x 0.1997 m: 2,182 faces (4,364 tris; budget 6,000)`
